name: Container lifecycle dependency attribution
problem: Classes loaded during shared test setup lack a test identity.
how: A container identity collects setup dependencies and unions them into member tests, with nested container frames and a bounded hidden-class window.

name: Bounded direct invocation fallback
problem: Cached string dispatch can hide a parser dependency from dynamic tracking.
how: The proposed optional rule expands selection from an executed class to its direct invocation owners and explains each extra selection.

name: Container lifecycle dependency attribution
problem: Shared setup, cleanup, and inter-test work can load dependencies outside a test identity.
how: The listener restores a container identity between tests and unions its dependencies into direct members; nested windows are suspended and restored.

name: Bounded direct invocation fallback
problem: Cached string dispatch can hide dependencies from dynamic tracking.
how: Direct invocation owners are recorded for dynamically executed classes and a changed target selects the test with an explainable reason.

name: Index storage boundary
problem: Both build plugins need consistent index persistence and safe missing-index behavior.
how: A generic keyed get and put interface separates index consumers from local and remote persistence.

name: Validator exclusion evidence boundary
problem: Known flaky tests can contaminate validation, while hidden exclusions can overstate evidence.
how: Explicit class exclusions apply to every target build and are recorded in validation reports.

name: Mutation-based selection validation
problem: Historical replay only observes regressions that happened in project history.
how: Bounded deterministic mutations create synthetic Git edges; confirmed killing tests are compared with selection using the shared replay analyzer.

name: Runtime dependency attribution
problem: A class loaded once can be reused by many tests without further class load events.
how: Instrumented project classes report runtime use under each active test identity so shared instances are attributed to every test that exercises them.

name: Tracking index integrity
problem: Incomplete tracking records can cause unsafe selection and empty tests can be mistaken for new tests.
how: Started tests receive baseline entries and an isolated tracking build persists its index only after success; failures trigger conservative fallback.

name: Matrix selection feedback
problem: Parallel JDK jobs need one consistent pull request summary and complete timing history.
how: Each matrix job publishes its report and a single downstream job aggregates the reports; timing data persists per module.

name: Maven selection modes
problem: CI needs to refresh dependencies on base builds and safely select tests on changes.
how: One Maven goal routes builds among tracking, selecting from an applicable index, and full-suite fallback.

name: Validator ground-truth build modes
problem: Repeated commit builds slow historical replay while agent instrumentation can affect the ground-truth oracle.
how: The default keeps agent-free ground truth and removes a duplicate probe; an explicit fast mode reuses agent-attached commit builds.

name: Commit-keyed dependency indexes
problem: A dependency index must correspond to the baseline used for change selection.
how: A resolved commit determines the storage key and its index anchor is checked before selection; mismatches trigger full-suite fallback.

name: Explained conservative test selection
problem: Changed source must select dependent tests while unobservable changes require a safe fallback.
how: The shared selection engine combines tracked dependencies, new tests, and conservative fallback rules into decisions with explicit reasons.

name: Parallel validator replay and durable build cache
problem: Historical validation repeatedly builds commits and consumes excessive time and memory.
how: Bounded worker pools reuse isolated checkouts and cache successful builds on disk; pair analysis loads results on demand and failed builds are retried on resume.

name: Mutation-based selection validation
problem: Validation needs mutation candidates from multi-module project source trees.
how: Candidate discovery walks conventional per-module production roots and retains repository-relative paths for module scoping.

name: Ambient dependency fallback
problem: Classes loaded outside individual test windows cannot always be attributed to a specific test.
how: The tracker records ambient dependencies and selection conservatively runs the suite when a changed class matches that set, with an explicit reason.

name: GitHub selection feedback
problem: Teams need selection results in CI without coupling the build plugin to GitHub credentials.
how: A composite action validates the portable report, writes a job summary, and updates a marked comment for eligible pull requests.

name: Gradle selection cache inputs
problem: Gradle must invalidate cached test tasks when the Git baseline or dependency index changes.
how: The plugin declares Git state and the index as task inputs, while tracking builds execute to produce fresh records.

name: Gradle test selection adapter
problem: Gradle builds need the shared test-selection engine applied to their test tasks.
how: The plugin discovers compiled tests before execution, invokes the shared selector, and applies test filters only when the index is usable.

name: Gradle tracking adapter
problem: Gradle test workers must produce a complete dependency index on baseline builds.
how: A self-contained agent attaches to test workers, whose records are merged into an anchored index after execution.

name: Inert change classification
problem: Documentation-only changes need not trigger test selection, while runtime resources must remain conservative.
how: A fixed path allowlist classifies inert files separately and excludes resource paths from that allowlist.

name: Versioned selection report and timing history
problem: CI needs an auditable selection report and credible time-saved estimates before test execution.
how: A versioned BuildReport records decisions and change context; prior Surefire timings yield a savings estimate only when skipped tests have complete history.

name: Runtime dependency attribution
problem: Discovery-loaded project classes lack a test identity at load time.
how: Project classes are instrumented to record later runtime use per test; classes that cannot be instrumented remain subject to ambient fallback.

name: Parallel validator replay and durable build cache
problem: Mutation validation over historical pairs is expensive and must remain deterministic and resumable.
how: Pairs run on bounded isolated checkouts, results are folded in input order, and completed mutation experiments are cached for resume.

name: Merge-base comparison
problem: A moving target branch can introduce unrelated changes into a pull request comparison.
how: Both adapters derive the diff and index lookup from the Git merge base; missing common ancestry falls back to the full suite.

name: Self-contained Maven plugin release
problem: Consumers need a standalone plugin without internal reactor dependencies or library conflicts.
how: The release packages core inside the plugin, relocates dependencies, and publishes a signed flattened artifact.

name: Historical mutation replay
problem: A standalone mutation run does not validate selection in the context of historical changes.
how: Each real baseline-to-head pair can produce bounded mutant children of its head; selection uses the baseline while confirmed killers are measured against the head.

name: Shared remote index storage
problem: Separate CI runners need access to the same commit-keyed dependency index.
how: An optional S3-compatible backend implements the shared index-store interface and uses standard credential discovery; unavailable indexes trigger safe fallback.

name: Historical replay evidence
problem: Adjacent graph traversal entries can represent nonexistent transitions and zero misses can hide a lack of observed failures.
how: Replay uses direct Git parent-child edges and reports newly confirmed failure coverage alongside misses and exclusions.

name: Historical mutation replay
problem: Building every reactor module for each isolated mutant is expensive.
how: Mutation builds scope to the owning module and its dependencies and dependents when the reactor graph establishes the scope; uncertain scope uses the full reactor.

name: Reactor-scoped fallback
problem: A non-source change can force the whole reactor to run even when its effects are confined to a module.
how: A reactor graph maps changes to owning modules and their transitive dependents; unknown scope falls back across the reactor.

name: Self-hosted CI selection
problem: The project needs CI to exercise the plugin built from the current checkout without creating a Maven reactor cycle.
how: CI bootstraps the plugin under a temporary coordinate, coordinates one reactor tracking run, and aggregates module reports.

name: Shadow-mode validation
problem: Test selection needs evidence that skipped tests would not have detected observed regressions.
how: The validator replays project history in disposable checkouts, compares selection with confirmed results from the target build, and reports would-miss cases.

name: Tracking agent runtime boundary
problem: The validator and the target test JVM can use different Java and JUnit versions.
how: Core tracking targets Java 17 and leaves JUnit Platform ownership to the target, while the validator retains its Java 21 baseline.

name: Reachable stale baseline selection
problem: An exact baseline index can be unavailable during a cache publication race.
how: The resolver chooses a valid reachable ancestor index and widens the diff from its anchor; without one, selection falls back to the full suite.

name: Test-boundary runtime tracking
problem: Virtual threads and hidden classes do not follow ordinary named class-load attribution.
how: Test identity propagates to child threads and hidden-class deltas are mapped to stable source names at test boundaries.

name: Kotlin source mapping and inline fallback
problem: Kotlin-generated JVM classes and inlined bodies do not map directly to source filenames.
how: Conventional Kotlin paths produce facade and nested-class candidates; potential inline functions use conservative fallback.

name: Versioned dependency index compatibility
problem: A persisted index from an unfamiliar schema cannot safely drive test selection.
how: Both build integrations check the shared format contract and use a named full-test fallback for incompatible data.
